descriptionChirho: To weigh down, make heavy, or burden, used almost exclusively in the passive in the NT to describe being weighed down or oppressed. The disciples' eyes were heavy with sleep in Gethsemane (Matt 26:43) and at the Transfiguration (Luke 9:32). Jesus warns against hearts being weighed down with dissipation (Luke 21:34). Paul describes being burdened beyond strength in Asia (2 Cor 1:8) and groaning under the burden of mortality (2 Cor 5:4). Paul instructs that the church not be burdened by supporting widows who have relatives (1 Tim 5:16). Multilingual glosses consistently use 'heavy/burdened': arb: مُثْقَلَة, heb: כְּבֵדוֹת/הֻכְבַּדְנוּ, kor: 무거웠다/눌렸다, spa: cargados, fra: alourdir/accabler.
